editorial:
Imagine being a teenage girl in the 1400s who suddenly believes God is talking to her, telling her to save all of France from the English. That is exactly where you start with this story. You get to follow Joan, a young woman with huge faith, as she convinces the King to let her lead his army into battle. The vibe here is very serious and slow, focusing more on her inner strength and her conversations with the church than on huge, flashy battle scenes. It feels more like a character study than a typical war movie, making you feel the weight of her burden as she tries to do what she thinks is right.

What really stands out is the acting, as you can tell Joan is truly torn between her faith and the people trying to trick her. The pacing is a bit slow for some, but the costume design and sets make it feel real. If you love history and stories about strong women, you will enjoy this. To get the best experience, you should stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for those crisp visuals, or maybe rent it on Apple TV if you want a quick watch. If you are a huge movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great call.
endingExplained: The movie ends on a heartbreaking note when the church refuses to listen to Joan's truth. After a long trial where they try to make her admit she was wrong, she stays true to her beliefs. You see her being led away to be burned at the stake. Even in her final moments, she does not give up her faith. She dies bravely, proving that her spirit was stronger than the people who judged her.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves historical dramas and stories about faith.
